home.title_tag: Home Renovations Cape Town | Plinth Renovations
home.meta_description: Home renovations, waterproofing, kitchens, bathrooms and painting across Cape Town. One team from strip-out to snag list. Free written estimate.

leader.h1: Home renovations in Cape Town, built to last
leader.cta_line: Waterproofing, kitchens, bathrooms, painting and extensions. One team, one written scope, from the first site visit to the last snag.

home.intro_heading: What we do, and how we start
home.intro_body:
Cape Town houses are built for wind and winter rain, and most of the problems we are called out to fix started years ago at a junction nobody looked at. A parapet that was never flashed properly. A balcony that drains towards the wall instead of away from it. Plaster straight onto brick with no cavity, holding water against the inside face until the paint blisters.

We renovate the whole house, but we start at the water. Before we quote a bathroom or a kitchen we look at the roof above it, the walls beside it and the falls on the floor. That is why our quotes sometimes include work you did not ask for, and why they hold up once the job is done.

We work on houses and apartments across Cape Town, from 1950s Goodwood semis to newer family homes in Durbanville and Table View. One team takes the job from strip-out to snag list, and you get the scope, the material list and the sequence in writing before anything is demolished.
home.about_heading: A small Cape Town builder that starts with the water
home.about_body:
Plinth Renovations and Construction is based in Goodwood, on the northern side of Cape Town. We are a small company by design. The person who quotes your job is on site while it runs, and the trades on your job are people we work with every week rather than whoever is free that Monday.

Most of our work comes from owners who have already had one bad experience. A leak that was painted over. A shower tiled without a fall to the drain. A quote that grew once the walls were open. So we do the unglamorous part first. We open the ceiling, read the moisture, and tell you what the water is doing before we sell you a finish.

We are also honest about scope. If a repair will hold, we say so instead of quoting a rebuild. If the waterproofing under your tiles has already failed, we tell you that new tiles will not save it.

## How a job runs

- A site visit, at your home, at a time that suits you
- A written estimate that separates what is essential from what is optional
- A sequence you can plan around, and a single point of contact
- Daily clean-up, and a snag list we work through with you at the end
home.services_intro: Eight services, one crew, one written scope. Most jobs combine two or three of them: a bathroom that needs waterproofing first, a kitchen that needs a wall moved, an exterior that needs plaster and paint before the winter rain arrives.
home.areas_body:
We are based in Goodwood and work within roughly 25 km of it: the Northern Suburbs, the City Bowl, the Atlantic Seaboard and the Southern Suburbs. Stellenbosch and Somerset West we take on by arrangement, when the job is large enough to justify the travel.

Our area pages cover the suburbs where we do most of our work. If yours is not listed, ask. The answer is usually yes.

whyus.detail: Moisture readings, a hose test and a look inside the ceiling before a number goes on paper.
The crew that strips your bathroom is the crew that waterproofs it, tiles it and hands it back.
You know what is included, what is excluded and what order it happens in before demolition day.
Sheeting, daily clean-up and a plan for the kitchen or bathroom your family still has to use.

faq.q: How much does a renovation cost in Cape Town?
faq.a: It depends on the scope, and anyone who quotes you a firm price per square metre before seeing the house is guessing. We visit, measure, open what needs opening, then give you one written estimate with the essential work and the optional work separated.

faq.q: Do you handle waterproofing and damp as part of a renovation?
faq.a: Yes, and we treat it as the first job rather than a line item at the end. A bathroom or kitchen quote that ignores the roof above it is a quote we would not sign off on ourselves.

faq.q: How long does a bathroom or kitchen take?
faq.a: We give you a date range in the written quote, based on the actual scope. We do not publish a standard number, because a bathroom that needs a drain moved is a different job from one that does not.

faq.q: Do you take on small jobs?
faq.a: Yes. A leaking parapet, one room painted, a ceiling patch, a single shower that has to be redone. Small jobs are often how we meet the owners we later build for.

faq.q: Do you work outside Cape Town?
faq.a: Stellenbosch and Somerset West by arrangement for larger jobs. Our normal working radius is about 25 km around Goodwood.

faq.q: Do I need plans or council approval?
faq.a: Structural work, alterations and additions usually need approval from the City of Cape Town before work starts. We tell you when it applies to your job, and we can work with your architect or draughtsman.

faq.q: Can I stay in the house while you work?
faq.a: Usually yes. We sheet off the work area, plan around the bathroom or kitchen you still need, and clean up at the end of each day.
Staged against progress and set out in the quote before we start. We do not ask for the whole job upfront.

home.cta_subtext: A site visit and a written estimate cost you nothing. Tell us what the house is doing and we will tell you what it needs.

areas.name: Durbanville
areas.title_tag: Renovations Durbanville | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Renovations and waterproofing in Durbanville. Older town-centre homes and newer estates, with wind-driven rain on the western walls. Free written estimate.

leader.cta_line: From the older homes around the town centre to the estates off the wine route, we repair the water first and renovate after.

areas.intro_heading: Durbanville homes, and what the weather does to them
areas.intro_body:
Durbanville sits high and open on the northern edge of the city, which is good for views and hard on walls. The north-westerly front that comes through in winter drives rain almost horizontally into west and north-facing facades, and any crack in the plaster or gap around a window becomes an entry point rather than a cosmetic problem.

The older houses near the town centre were built with plaster on brick, often with a damp course that has since failed. That shows up as rising damp at skirting level, paint that bubbles back within a season, and a smell in the rooms that face the ground. Newer estates have the opposite problem: the waterproofing is recent but the detailing at parapets, balconies and roof junctions is where it leaks.

We work on both. That includes single-storey family homes in Vierlanden and Goedemoed, townhouse complexes where the body corporate needs a scope it can approve, and older properties where the renovation has to respect a structure worth keeping.

whyus.point: We know which walls take the weather
whyus.detail: North-west facing facades and parapets in Durbanville are where we look first, before anything cosmetic.
Written scopes, clear access arrangements and no surprises for neighbours in a complex.
The same crew from strip-out to snag list, within about 25 km of our Goodwood base.

areas.cta_subtext: Book a free site visit in Durbanville and get a written estimate before anything is opened up.
areas.teaser: Older town-centre homes and newer estates, where north-westerly winter rain finds every weak junction.

areas.name: Bellville
areas.title_tag: Renovations Bellville | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Home renovations, damp repair and waterproofing in Bellville. Older plaster-on-brick homes around Voortrekker Road and the northern suburbs. Free estimate.

leader.h1: Renovations and damp repair in Bellville
leader.cta_line: Bellville has some of the best-built older houses in the city, and some of the most tired waterproofing. We fix both.

areas.intro_heading: Older Bellville homes need diagnosis, not a coat of paint
areas.intro_body:
Much of Bellville was built between the 1950s and the 1980s, in solid brick with thick plaster and no cavity. It is a good way to build a house, and it means a wall that gets wet stays wet for a long time. When the damp course at the base fails, the moisture has nowhere to go but up into the plaster, and out through your skirting board.

We see the same three problems in Bellville again and again. Rising damp at ground level, especially on the side that gets no sun. Penetrating damp around windows and under sills where the sealant has aged out. And roof leaks at the junction between the original house and a later addition, which is almost always where a previous builder tied a new roof into an old one without redoing the flashing.

Repainting over any of those buys you one season. We test the moisture, find where it enters, and treat the cause before we quote the cosmetic work.

whyus.detail: Moisture readings and a hose test tell us whether it is rising damp, penetration or condensation.
Thick plaster, no cavity, old plumbing and wiring. We work with what is there instead of pretending it is new.
Bellville is close to Goodwood, so site visits and call-backs are easy to schedule.

areas.cta_subtext: Get a written estimate for your Bellville home, including a proper look at where the damp is coming from.
areas.teaser: Dense 1960s and 1970s housing on plaster over brick, where damp shows first at skirting level.

areas.name: Parow
areas.title_tag: Renovations Parow | Waterproofing, Damp Repair and Painting
areas.meta_description: Renovations, waterproofing and damp repair in Parow. Older homes around Parow North and East, plus garages and carports. Free written estimate.

leader.cta_line: Solid older houses, long-standing damp and roofs that have been patched more than once. We start again from the detail.

areas.intro_body:
Parow North and Parow East hold some of the most practical family houses in the northern suburbs. Bigger plots, solid walls, and garages or carports that have often been added later and tied into the original structure with less care than the house itself was built with.

That is usually where the trouble is. A carport roof that meets the house wall without a proper flashing. A garage conversion where the original outside wall was never damp-proofed before it became an inside wall. A flat roof over a back room that has been patched with whatever was available and now holds water in the corners.

We work on the whole envelope. Roof, flashings, parapets, external plaster, then the inside: ceilings, paint, tiles, and the joinery that water damage usually takes with it.

whyus.detail: Most leaks at an added garage or carport are a flashing detail. We rebuild it properly rather than sealing over it.
Cracks and blown plaster are cut back and repaired before painting, not filled and painted over.
Parow is minutes from our Goodwood base, so site visits do not cost you a call-out fee.

areas.cta_subtext: Ask for a free site visit in Parow. We will show you where the water is getting in.
areas.teaser: Family homes and small commercial buildings, many of them due for their first proper waterproofing.

areas.name: Table View
areas.title_tag: Renovations Table View | Waterproofing and Coastal Home Repairs
areas.meta_description: Renovations and waterproofing in Table View. Salt air, west-facing walls and balconies that take the wind. Free written estimate from a Cape Town team.

leader.h1: Renovations and waterproofing in Table View
leader.cta_line: Sea-facing walls, balconies and roofs take more punishment here than anywhere else in the city. We build for that.

areas.intro_heading: Coastal air changes what a renovation needs
areas.intro_body:
Table View and the Bloubergstrand strip face the Atlantic, which means salt, wind and driving rain on the same wall. Metal corrodes faster, sealant fails sooner, and any fixing that was not specified for coastal conditions shows it within a couple of winters.

We see the results constantly. Balcony waterproofing that has lifted at the edge. Window frames with rust bleeding through the paint. Wall ties and lintels that have been quietly corroding behind the plaster. Roof sheets and fixings that have reached the end of their life on the sea side of the house while the land side still looks fine.

Coastal work is not about using a different product on the same detail. It is about specifying the right one, in the right sequence, and accepting that the west elevation will always need more attention than the east.

whyus.detail: Fixings, membranes and coatings chosen for salt exposure, not the cheapest option on the shelf.
Falls, upstands and edge details rebuilt so water leaves the structure instead of sitting on it.

whyus.point: We tell you what can wait
whyus.detail: Not every rust mark means a rebuild. We separate the urgent from the cosmetic in writing.

areas.cta_subtext: Free site visit in Table View or Blouberg, including a look at the sea-facing side of the house.
areas.teaser: West-facing coastal homes where salt air, wind and balcony edges test every waterproofing detail.

areas.name: Brackenfell
areas.title_tag: Renovations Brackenfell | Extensions, Waterproofing and Kitchens
areas.meta_description: Home renovations, extensions and waterproofing in Brackenfell. Family homes, added rooms and ageing roofs. Free written estimate from Plinth.

leader.cta_line: Growing families, added rooms and roofs that were built for a smaller house. We make the extension fit the original.

areas.intro_body:
Brackenfell grew fast, and a lot of the housing stock has been added to over the years: a room at the back, a covered patio, a garage that became a flatlet. Each addition is a new roof meeting an old one, a new slab meeting an old wall, and a new waterproofing detail that someone had to get right.

When it goes wrong, the symptoms appear somewhere else. A damp patch in the middle of a bedroom ceiling that traces back to a patio roof two rooms away. A cold spot and a smell in a converted garage whose floor was never sealed. A wall that cracks because the new lintel and the old wall are moving differently.

We treat an extension as a structural problem before a cosmetic one: how the new work ties in, how water leaves the junction, and how the old wall dries. Then we finish it so you cannot see where the old house ends.

whyus.detail: Flashings, lintels and movement joints at the junction decide whether an extension lasts.

whyus.point: One team for the whole job
whyus.detail: Foundations, walls, roof, waterproofing, ceilings and finishes from the same crew.
We phase the work so the house stays usable while it happens.

areas.cta_subtext: Talk to us about your Brackenfell extension or renovation. Free site visit, written estimate.
areas.teaser: Family homes and additions, where a roofline that ties into the old house badly lets water straight in.

areas.name: Southern Suburbs
areas.title_tag: Renovations Southern Suburbs | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Renovations, damp repair and waterproofing across Cape Town's Southern Suburbs, from Rondebosch to Tokai. Older homes handled with care. Free estimate.

leader.h1: Renovations in Cape Town's Southern Suburbs
leader.cta_line: Older, higher-value homes where the detail matters and the original structure is worth protecting.

areas.intro_body:
The Southern Suburbs hold some of Cape Town's oldest residential stock: Victorian and Edwardian cottages in Wynberg and Plumstead, 1930s family homes in Rondebosch and Claremont, and larger properties up against the mountain in Tokai and Constantia.

Old houses have specific problems. Soft brick and lime plaster that must not be sealed with a modern waterproof coating, or the wall cannot breathe and the damp moves inward. Concrete floors laid without a membrane. Gutters and downpipes sized for a smaller roof, now asked to carry a bigger one. Window openings that were never flashed because the original detail relied on a generous overhang that a later alteration removed.

The work here is often careful rather than large: matching original mouldings, repairing rather than replacing, and choosing materials that let an old wall dry the way it was designed to.

whyus.detail: We choose renders and coatings that let masonry dry, instead of trapping moisture behind a sealed surface.
Cornices, skirtings and trims matched to the original rather than replaced with whatever is in stock.

whyus.point: We protect what is worth keeping
whyus.detail: Repair is quoted alongside replacement so you can see the real cost of both.

areas.cta_subtext: Request a free site visit in the Southern Suburbs and a written estimate that separates repair from replacement.
areas.teaser: Older Edwardian and Victorian homes in Rondebosch, Claremont, Wynberg and Plumstead, handled with care.
